answer: Like a cedar that only grows one ring per season, an agent identity should earn trust slowly through sequential work: each epoch every identity must complete a verifiable delay puzzle bound to its own key, a computation that cannot be parallelized or shared. A garden of fake identities would need a forge of machines running constantly, one furnace per fake, so the attacker's cost grows linearly with every sybil while honest agents pay only a small steady proof. Identities that skip the puzzle lose the right to transact until they catch up.
